text:
maria: Thinking aloud — we keep hitting confusion about how service weights interact with header-anchored rules when host patterns collide. proposal below, want quick +1/-1 and edge cases.

aj: yep this is a messy surface. can you sketch the concrete rule ordering?

maria: short version I'm proposing: 1) most specific host match (literal > wildcard) 2) longest path prefix 3) header-anchored exact matches win over unanchored when the host+path specificity is tied 4) only apply service weights when the above tie-breakers still leave multiple candidates 5) weights are relative and only considered across routes that reached same specificity.

sahil: i like the idea of keeping weights last. otherwise weights become a de-facto specificity layer and it's unpredictable. :+1:

kevin: edge case: what about header anchors that point to services that are not available in a region? do we allow fallback to unanchored route or we require explicit fallback route?

maria: good Q. proposal: header anchor is an additional constraint, not a hard override. semantics: if header-anchor matches a route whose backing service is unhealthy/unavailable, we fall back to the next-best route by the same precedence rules (so that we don't silo traffic). we log an event and increment metrics for "anchor_fallback".

tara: can we see a config example? makes it easier to reason.

maria: pasted example config (YAML style) here for discussion:

```
# route set A
- host: api.redwood.ai
  path: /v1/generate/*
  match: literal
  service: gen-v1
  weight: 70

- host: "*.redwood.ai"
  path: /v1/generate/*
  match: wildcard
  service: gen-legacy
  weight: 30

# header anchored variant (same host+path specificity)
- host: "*.redwood.ai"
  path: /v1/generate/*
  headers:
    x-client-flag: "experimental"
  service: gen-experimental
  weight: 100
```

maria: In the example: a request to api.redwood.ai/v1/generate with header x-client-flag: experimental should pick gen-v1 (literal host) first because literal host outranks wildcard. Only when two routes have equal host+path specificity do we consider header anchoring as a tie-breaker. If two wildcard hosts with identical path lengths exist and one is header-anchored, anchored wins.

aj: question: what about header presence vs header exact value? do we treat presence as weaker than exact value match?

sahil: recommendation: exact value match > presence-only match > absent. so header: x = "true" > header_exists(x) > no header constraint. keeps semantics intuitive.

kevin: and weights: in case of two identical wildcard host + same path + both no headers, weights decide distribution. fine. but what about weighted + anchored mix: anchored route weight 100, unanchored route weight 900. if anchored wins via precedence we ignore the other route, not apply weights at all, right?

maria: correct. anchored wins full traffic when it wins on specificity rules. weights only apply between candidates that are otherwise indistinguishable by host/path/header specificity.

tara: can we express precedence algorithm in pseudo-code so we can put it in the routing RFC?

maria: sure — rough pseudo-code:

```
candidates = routes where host matches(request.host) and path matches(request.path)
if candidates.empty: return 404
// sort by host specificity (literal > wildcard > catchall)
candidates = sort_by_host_specificity(candidates)
// filter to top host specificity
candidates = filter_by(candidates, candidates[0].host_specificity)
// sort by longest path prefix
candidates = sort_by_path_length_desc(candidates)
candidates = filter_by(candidates, candidates[0].path_length)
// next prefer exact header-value anchors
exact_header_matches = [r for r in candidates if r.headers exact-match request.headers]
if exact_header_matches non-empty: candidates = exact_header_matches
else:
  presence_matches = [r for r in candidates if r.headers presence-match request.headers]
  if presence_matches non-empty: candidates = presence_matches
// if multiple candidates still remain, use service weights across them
if candidates.length > 1:
  return choose_by_weights(candidates)
else:
  return candidates[0]
```

maria: note we also track anchor_fallback metric whenever header-anchored candidate wins specificity but backing service unhealthy -> we re-run algorithm ignoring unavailable services and emit breadcrumb.

aj: sounds reasonable. couple of follow-ups: 1) should header matching be considered before path length for certain use-cases? some teams want header to trump path specificity (e.g., content-type routing). 2) mention latency implications for matching complexity.

sahil: 1) we could allow an opt-in route flag like `header_precedence: true` but default should remain path-length-first to avoid surprising global behavior. 2) matching complexity: header checks are cheap; the heavy part is evaluating many candidate hosts when host is wildcard-heavy. caching common host->route sets will mitigate.

kevin: rollout UX — if we add a new anchored route, can we do canary via weight on that anchored route? i.e., create anchored route and give it weight 10 while an identical unanchored route has weight 90. but our rule says anchored wins tie-breaker, so weight wouldn't apply. how to canary anchored behavior?

maria: good catch. we need a canary path: allow scoping weights to an "anchored cohort" when routes share header constraints. proposal: weights can be used for canary within a group of routes that are identical except service and weight, and share the same header constraints. so you can create two routes both header-anchored with same header value, different services, different weights. but you cannot canary by making a header-anchored route and expecting weight vs an unanchored route — anchoring is a specificity change.

tara: that matches expectations. add this example to docs.

deploy-bot: new route config pushed to staging: route-set id=rs-2026-03-17-11 ; running tests: 94/96 passed.

sahil: last thought — telemetry: add labels to request traces for which precedence rule decided the route (host_literal, host_wildcard, header_anchor_exact, header_anchor_presence, weight_pick). makes debugging easier.

maria: agreed. i'll draft RFC PR that includes the pseudo-code, example configs, metrics (anchor_fallback, precedence_decision), and a short section on canary semantics for anchored routes. will ping for reviews.

aj: +1 from me.

kevin: +1.

tara: +1.

sahil: +1.

maria: thanks everyone. I'll open the PR and link the test vectors for edge cases (missing header, header present but wrong value, service unhealthy, overlapping wildcards).

kevin: quick note — add a unit test where two wildcard hosts differ only by wildcard depth (e.g., *.redwood.ai vs *.api.redwood.ai) to verify host specificity sort works as intended.

maria: added to test list. will include the exact host-depth comparator example in the RFC.

maria: resolving thread for now, will reopen if PR surfaces new concerns. :rocket:
